articles.title: “I Hope You All Rot”: Pat McAfee Calls Out Critics for Making a Big Deal Out of Jason Kelce’s Blunder
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles lost 27-7 to the Chicago Bears in an upset. Even though the former were pretty much lackluster during the game, former Eagles offensi...
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles lost 27-7 to the Chicago Bears in an upset. Even though the former were pretty much lackluster during the game, former Eagles offensive lineman and franchise icon Jason Kelce still batted for his team during the Monday Night Countdown broadcast.

Kelce, while talking about the team, kept referring to it as 'we.'

"We played well offensively, we had opportunities, we shot ourselves in the foot," he said before continuing on. Pat McAfee, who was sitting right next to him on the desk, joked about Kelce's heavy usage of the word, saying it was a "lot of 'we' talk" out of Jason.

Kelce had apologized right there for his mistake, but former ESPN host Ryan Clark took a shot at him:

"I'm trying to mind my own, but hell yea it's 'We' Future Hall of Famer!!," he wrote on X. "… Blood, sweat, tears, & glory in Philly. No one can take that away. You can still do your job the right way! Bump anyone saying differently."

But McAfee, probably in reference to this comment (as stated by Awful Announcing), stepped in to defend Jason Kelce.

"Now, I usually mind my own, but if you thought I was being serious whenever I pointed out Jason Kelce was saying 'we' about the Philadelphia Eagles, knowing who Jason Kelce is, with the Philadelphia Eagles at the Monday Night Football halftime, you have no brain, and I think you should just realize that," McAfee clarified on The Pat McAfee Show on September 30, 2026.

"I don't love just the lying and the stuff that happens on my name these days, but just saying stuff to continue to add gas to a flame that isn't real when you're in this place and carry as much weight as you definitely do, I think it's a little bit of a piling on, and I hope you all rot. All of you."

Fan reactions to Kelce's error have been mixed. There are quite a few who say it wasn't really a problem, since they understood that Kelce played for the Eagles his entire career.

Kelce's love for Philly will always be unmatched. He played for the Eagles from 2011 to 2023, and was perhaps one of the franchise's best offensive linemen in history. Fans love him, and he has never shied away from sharing his love for Philadelphia.

However, as a broadcaster, one should not be taking sides with their former team. For what it's worth, Kelce wasn't glazing the team entirely. But saying 'we' that many times put him in the same camp. McAfee only laughed at Kelce after pointing out his mistake.

The former OL is currently in his third year of being on Monday Night Countdown, and has done pretty well so far. It is unlikely that the slip-up would warrant any action, as it was all well and good after Kelce apologized.

The game would eventually turn out to be a nightmare for Eagles fans, as backup QB Case Keenum stunned Philadelphia into a defeat. The veteran signal-caller last played in the 2023 season prior to this game and played like he never lost his mojo.

Perhaps when he is on the panel during the next Eagles game, Jason Kelce will be wary of siding too much for his beloved team.

articles.title: Luke Humphries races into World Grand Prix quarter-finals
articles.summary: Luke Humphries makes it through to the World Grand Prix quarter-finals, along with James Wade, Gian van Veen and Niels Zonneveld.
articles.body:
Luke Humphries has made it through to the World Grand Prix quarter-finals, along with James Wade, Gian van Veen and Niels Zonneveld.

World number two Humphries, who won the tournament in 2023 and was beaten by the eliminated Luke Littler in last year's final, was a comfortable 3-0 winner against Jermaine Wattimena in Leicester.

The Englishman, who hit three 180s and had a highest checkout of 129, will play the Netherlands' Zonneveld, who beat Gary Anderson 3-1, in the last eight.

"It wasn't the best performance, but it was a good performance," Humphries told Sky Sports.

"I think I got in every time with my first three [darts]. When you are doing stuff like that, it is going to take a top performance to beat you.

"I've got a good chance of winning this. At the moment I am a bit up and down, but if I can put that right I am going to be tough to beat."

Wade has won the World Grand Prix twice - in 2007 and 2010 - and kept his hopes of a third title intact with a 3-1 win against Stephen Bunting.

In a tournament where you have to start and finish each leg with a double, Wade took the first two sets and, despite losing the next, won the fourth to secure victory.

Van Veen, who was beaten by Littler in the PDC World Championship final in January and could become world number two unless Humphries wins the title, won the first set against Ryan Searle but then found himself 2-1 down.

He recovered to level before taking the decider to set up a quarter-final against Wade.

articles.title: Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is thoroughly impressed by Aleksandar Pavlović
articles.summary: Is Pavlović ready to take over from Joshua Kimmich for FC Bayern and Germany?
articles.body:
Germany's second squad in the international break dazzled all with their conviction and repaid the new German coach Jürgen Klopp with a 2-0 victory over Serbia. Bayern Munich's Aleksandar Pavlović received a special shoutout from his manager for his efforts.

The 22 year-old midfielder was a reliable central piece to Klopp's high tempo playstyle. Overlapping runs, diagonal crosses, dribbles and shots from wingers, counter-pressing defense along with a sweeping goalkeeper. At the center of it all was Pavlović, who was the glue that ensured the ball was received and fed to the most productive channel.

And for having facilitated that central role exceptionally well, Jürgen Klopp could not hold back his praise for Pavlović. "What a game by Pavlović. He was everywhere!" exclaimed Klopp ( ZDF via @iMiaSanMia ) after the third Nations League game of this international window.

Pavlović was the go-to man for his team, registering a game high 148 touches and making 123 passes with a remarkable 93 percent accuracy. He combined his machine-like passing ability with his attacking vision to create three chances.

The midfielder has been working on his defensive skillset as well. Against a robust Serbian side committed to physical challenges, Pavlović's recoveries and 60 percent duel success allowed Germany to retain and dominate possession. Pavlović was a vital cog of the stable base upon which Klopp's intense attacking brand of football could play out on the pitch.

articles.title: Thursday playoff discussion thread
articles.summary: Today’s docket: Phillies at Braves.
articles.body:
We have for you another Thursday baseball discussion thread, but this time, featuring 100% more playoffs! Which, of course, means no Royals 🙁

Only one game today as three of the four Wild Card series ended in sweeps yesterday.

First, the White Sox knocked out the Astros. Crane's Boys are out! No great shock.

The Yankees disposed of the Red Sox last evening. Not much of a series as the nonJudgemental Yankees smoked Boston to the tune of 18-2 over two games.

Lastly, the Padres swept the Cubs, winning last night 4-1. I hope you agree with me that the playoffs just became 10 times more enjoyable with the Cubs eliminated.

The only series left is Philadelphia vs Atlanta. The Braves took game one on Tuesday 5-3 with three runs in the bottom of the eighth. Last night, the Phillies scored twice in the top of the eighth to tie the game at 3-3 before winning it in extras, 4-3. Alec Bohm, somewhat of a local kid—went to high school in Omaha before attending Wichita State—hit a home run in the top of the tenth to give the Phillies a lead it would not relinquish.

The pitching matchup will be Aaron Nola for the Phillies against Ray Kerr for the Braves.

Nola, a 12-year vet, all with Philadelphia, finished the season only 7-12 with a 4.67 ERA (3% below league average) and a 4.87 FIP. He also allowed the most home runs with 37. This will be his 12th career playoff start.

The Braves counter with Ray Kerr, more of an Opener than a Starter. The 31-year-old lefty only opened one game for the Braves this season, which was his last outing against the Marlins. He fared well, going three innings in which he walked one, allowed two hits, but didn't give up any runs. He only pitched in nine games this season, but in that limited action, which totaled 18-and-1/3 innings, he sported a 1.47 ERA, 3.97 FIP while striking out 11 and walking two.

More importantly, Kerr faced the Phillies twice in September, and held them scoreless over both outings. In those two appearances, he pitched 6-and-1/3 innings, allowed two hits while walking zero batters and striking out five. None of his four inherited runners came around to score.

Kerr has never before pitched in the playoffs.

You can catch the game on NBC or Peacock at 7:00 p.m. CDT.

articles.title: Evaluating the Oklahoma Sooners at their bye week
articles.summary: Taking stock of OU's 2026 season so far at the bye week.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners are on their bye week this week, taking a break after a rocky first month of the season . OU is currently 2-2 overall and 0-1 in the SEC to begin the 2026 season, and a year that began with very high expectations is teetering on the brink of falling apart.

After this off week, OU will play eight straight SEC games, so this is the only chance head coach Brent Venables and the Sooners have to catch their breath before the end of the regular season. With the way this year has gone so far, Oklahoma absolutely has to use this open date to improve in a big way.

The season started innocently enough, as Oklahoma won its season-opener at home 51-0 over the UTEP Miners in Week 1. Strong performances on both offense and defense led the way against an overmatched opponent, but it was exactly what Sooner Nation wanted to see to start the season.

Things quickly went sideways, however. OU's first test of the season came on the road against the Michigan Wolverines in Week 2. Despite being favored, Oklahoma left Ann Arbor with a 17-10 loss that dampened all the preseason hype. The new offensive identity shown in the opener was gone, and the duo of offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle and quarterback John Mateer looked overwhelmed. The Sooners focused on physicality and running the ball the following week, and many hoped it would be a blip on the radar for an improving offense.

Week 3 saw Oklahoma host the New Mexico Lobos, and though the Sooners escaped with a 14-6 win, nobody around the program was happy with the victory. The offense was completely stuck in the mud and struggled to find any semblance of an identity. A great performance from the defense saved the day, but clearly OU had problems. Arbuckle and Mateer weren't as advertised; the offensive line was poor, the passing game was ineffective, and the running game was invisible. Still, OU was 2-1, with a big test on the horizon in the SEC opener.

Things fell apart in the Sooners' Week 4 loss on the road against the Georgia Bulldogs. The game wasn't even that close, and four turnovers doomed the Sooners. Three of those giveaways were courtesy of Mateer, who looked rattled all game long. Venables and Arbuckle stuck with him for the full game, and the offense once again lacked an identity.

After the bye, Oklahoma heads into the Red River Rivalry contest against the Texas Longhorns next week at the Cotton Bowl in Dallas. The 'Horns will also be coming off of their bye week, and they are undefeated and ranked No. 1 in the nation. This is essentially the opposite of a get-right game for the Sooners, and they have a lot to get right.

At the top of that list is the offense, which has regressed from last year. The Sooners have spent the better part of a month trying to find an identity on that side of the ball, and nothing has been figured out. Arbuckle and Mateer will take most of the blame, and they both have to be a lot better, but the offensive line has struggled throughout September. That has led to a poor running game and a predictable passing game, and the Sooners simply have to find something that they can do reasonably well on offense.

Venables' defense has been very good. However, tackling was a problem for the two games of the season, and with the margin of error this defense is being given by their offense, there simply can't be mistakes. Still, it's hard to heap too much judgment on the defense, as they are essentially being asked to win games by themselves right now.

Special teams coordinator Doug Deakin's unit hasn't been bad, but they've made some uncharacteristic mistakes that have hurt the Sooners. Tate Sandell, the best kicker in America last year, has missed his last two field goals. Isaiah Sategna III muffed a punt against New Mexico that could have easily cost OU if the defense hadn't had his back. The Sooners made a punter change against Georgia, as Jacob Ulrich started in place of Grayson Miller for the first time in over a year. Last season, special teams the difference for Oklahoma in a very positive way. This year's group has to get back to playing that way.

OU also needs to get healthy, as a number of impact players have missed significant time. Not having key players like Trell Harris, Michael Fasusi, Kip Lewis, Cole Sullivan, and Michael Boganowski for at least one full game (most for much longer) has hurt the Sooners in the first third of the season. Getting guys back on the field needs to be another priority for this team.

Overall, just about nothing has gone right this season in Norman. Ultimately, the product on the field falls at the feet of Venables and general manager Jim Nagy. They put this team together, and it isn't performing nearly well enough.

There are still eight games left, and Oklahoma can still turn the season around if they get a lot better in a short amount of time. The College Football Playoff is probably already out of reach, but a strong season is technically still possible. At the other end of the spectrum, the OU we've seen for the last three games will be lucky to make a bowl game, and the Sooners could be staring down their worst record in a long, long time in a season that began with so much promise.

articles.title: Wayne Gretzky, TNT pay tribute to Barry Melrose to open NHL season
articles.summary: The 2026–27 NHL season got started this week with the larger hockey world still mourning the death of beloved former player, coach, and analyst Barry Melrose...
articles.body:
The 2026–27 NHL season got started this week with the larger hockey world still mourning the death of beloved former player, coach, and analyst Barry Melrose .

Melrose was the face of hockey at ESPN for nearly three decades, and the Worldwide Leader paid fitting tribute to him on the opening night of the season , with his silhouette donning one of the walls of the network's new Studio W.

On Wednesday, TNT's first night of hockey coverage for the season, the competing network also took a moment to remember Melrose and all of his contributions to the sport.

Wayne Gretzky, who played under Melrose during his time with the Los Angeles Kings, had some touching words to remember his former coach.

"When you look at his picture, that's how he really was in life. He was always smiling. It could be the worst game we ever played. I remember one night, I think we lost 12–2, I think we outshot them 60–15 in the old Cow Palace. Kelly Hrudey was in goal. And after the game I was standing there, I hadn't come back yet from my injury, and Barry just stood up in front of the guys and said, 'I don't know what to say to you guys. I thought you had a great game.' And he walked out."

It's an anecdote that's easy for any fan of Melrose's to imagine. As Gretzky put it, he simply loved the game of hockey.

"He's always positive. If you were a fourth line guy or a fifth or sixth defenseman, he loved just coaching everyone, and he was positive every single day. Never had a bad moment. Loved coming to the rink. Loved being around the players. Gosh, the game's going to miss him. There was a big stretch there were he was the big voice for hockey in the United States, and in Canada. He will be sorely missed because he was so positive. Everywhere he went people loved him."

It was a nice moment between what are ostensibly competing networks to come together and pay respect to one of the most important figures in the growth of the sport in America.

articles.title: Chargers' Mike McDaniel admits offense has helped cost Chargers games
articles.summary: Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel takes full accountability for the struggling offense amid their 0-3 start.
articles.body:
Chargers coordinator Mike McDaniel recently took ownership of the team's struggling offense amid their 0-3 start to the season.

McDaniel spoke to reporters Thursday and said he shares some blame for the team's slow start, especially on offense.

"I'm fully responsible," McDaniel said . "… I spend zero time trying to avoid blame. It's quite the opposite."

McDaniel was hired as Los Angeles' new offensive coordinator earlier this year after he was fired as the Dolphins ' head coach. Although his time in Miami ended on a low note, the expectation coming into LA, with Justin Herbert under center, was that he was going to revolutionize the offense like no other.

Many tagged Herbert and McDaniel as one of the best coach-QB duos of the season. Instead, their offense looks confusing and flat-out awful through the first three weeks.

"I'm not minimizing it; it's not acceptable to me," he said of the offense. "But also not creating a fake gland that ignores annual history," he said. "There's a team that you guys can think of right now, either way, that everyone was crowning."

The Chargers rank near the bottom of several offensive categories, including 20th in total offense, 21st in passing yards per game, 17th in rushing yards per game, and 29th in points per game.

The Chargers' offense has been dreadful, but McDaniel is not backing down from the challenge. He said his job now is to make surey want the results the hit the field, and he insists he's living in reality rather than hope.

"There are things we've done in the past three games that are active participation in losing the game," he said. "And so flat-out our jobs are going to prove everything, and I'm not living in hope, I'm living in reality."

The Chargers have the opportunity to showcase their growth against a stout defense in the Seahawks.

articles.title: Eagles star misses second straight practice as lingering injury threatens Week 4 status
articles.summary: Eagles star is out again.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA — Eagles star wide receiver DeVonta Smith has missed two consecutive days of practice with a hamstring injury.

Smith first appeared on the injury report last week, but he played through his hamstring injury during the Eagles' blowout loss to the Chicago Bears on Monday.

According to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo, it sounds like Smith's status for the Eagles ' Week 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday is "legitimately questionable."

If Smith can't play against the Rams, the Eagles will start Dontayvion Wicks , Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper at wide receiver.

On Thursday, depth wide receiver Hollywood Brown also missed his second practice of the week with an ankle injury. Brown was ruled out before Monday's game against the Bears.

Smith has thrived as the Eagles' No. 1 wide receiver in the first three games of the season, recording 19 catches for 235 yards and one touchdown.

He has made spectacular catches, including snagging a 30-yard contested catch down field on Bears Pro Bowler Jaylon Johnson .

The Eagles' passing offense is struggling with Smith in the lineup, and those struggles would only get worse if he can't play.

On Sunday, the Eagles could have a hard time moving the ball against the Rams' defense.

New Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion must get Lemon going against the Rams. The first-round rookie wide receiver has finished with seven catches for 38 yards in the first three games.

Wicks would take over as the Eagles' No. 1 wide receiver. He has recorded nine catches for 179 yards and one touchdown.

articles.title: Bears Receive Concerning Injury News Regarding RB D’Andre Swift
articles.summary: The Bears have one key member on the offense who missed practice on Thursday due to a knee injury, putting his status for the Jets game in doubt. The post Be...
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears released the injury report on Thursday with a new face on the list — running back D'Andre Swift.

"#Bears RB D'Andre Swift (knee, DNP) is an addition to the team's injury report today," Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune posted on X. "He was not listed Wednesday when the team issued an 'estimation' for a walk-through."

Being a non-participant on Thursday is worrisome, but the hope is Swift is a full go for Sunday.

Bears RB D'Andre Swift Misses Practice, Along With Several Others

D'Andre Swift isn't the only Bears player who missed practice Thursday.

Braxton Jones also has a knee injury and did not practice; Caleb Williams is still recovering from his Grade 2 hamstring, and Cam Lewis (hip), Noah Sewell (Achilles), and Shemar Turner (knee) were all limited.

Grady Jarrett and Joe Thuney had rest days, so nothing concerning there. But the fact that Swift wasn't on Wednesday's estimated injury report and did not practice Thursday is a cause for concern.

Swift commented on the mystery behind who will start at quarterback against the New York Jets on Sunday, saying, "with how detailed that room is and with the job assignments and how they are, they kind of control the huddle when they're in there. When they hand them opportunities, they all do a great job. Whoever they put out there, we have the utmost belief that they're going to be able to get the job done."

Ben Johnson Comments on What Caleb Williams Can Learn From Case Keenum

The silver lining for Caleb Williams not playing in Monday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles was that he had the chance to see how a veteran operates the Bears' offense.

Williams hasn't missed a game since joining the Bears, and head coach Ben Johnson commented on his thoughts on what Caleb can learn from watching Keenum.

"There's a tremendous amount to be gained, even though he didn't participate last week, from taking a step back and seeing a big-picture lens of how the entire team was preparing, to specifically a different guy getting the keys to the car and seeing how he was going about his business and getting ready to drive it. I think I alluded to it after the game, just that quarterback meeting we have before the game is huge for us, and it was different. We don't want to be somebody that we're not, ultimately, and yet we can learn so much from the people that we're around."

articles.summary: Jeff Teague has changed his view on the Caitlin Clark and Olivia Miles debate after watching the two rookies handle the WNBA playoffs.
articles.body: Jeff Teague has changed his view on the Caitlin Clark and Olivia Miles debate after watching the two rookies handle the WNBA playoffs. On the latest episode of the Club 520 Podcast, the former NBA guard watched Clark’s 27-point, 15-assist performance against the Las Vegas Aces and said, “Olivia Miles is not better than Caitlin Clark.” Teague had sounded different before the playoffs, when he praised Miles while watching Clark. The change comes after Miles struggled against the New York Liberty, while Clark delivered a big Game 2 performance to keep the Indiana Fever alive.Jeff Teague changes his Caitlin Clark and Olivia Miles viewTeague’s latest comments came while he was breaking down Clark’s Game 2 performance against the Aces. Clark finished with 27 points, 15 assists and seven rebounds as the Fever won 99-89 at Gainbridge Fieldhouse.While watching Clark’s plays, Teague said:“Olivia Miles is not better than Caitlin Clark.”That was different from what Teague said last month. While watching Clark highlights at the time, he compared her with Miles and said:“Even the way she play, it don’t look like Olivia Miles, but she’s still cold.”The timing of Teague’s latest comment is important because the playoffs have given both players a very different setting from the regular season.Miles had a standout rookie campaign with the Minnesota Lynx. She broke Clark’s previous single-season rookie scoring record of 769 points, finishing with 790. Miles averaged 19.8 points, 4.7 rebounds and 6.0 assists while shooting close to 50% from the field.She also became an All-Star starter and won all four Rookie of the Month awards. But her first playoff series did not go the same way.Olivia Miles struggles as Caitlin Clark steps up for FeverThe Lynx were swept by the New York Liberty in the first round. Miles had 11 points and eight rebounds in Game 1 before scoring only five points on 1-of-8 shooting in Game 2. She played 17 minutes and was not on the floor at the end of the game.Clark also had a difficult start to the playoffs. In Game 1 against the Aces, she posted 15 points and 10 assists despite the Fever's loss.Game 2 was a different story. With Indiana facing elimination, Clark took control and helped the Fever force another game with her 27-point, 15-assist and seven-rebound performance.The difference is also understandable given their experience. Clark is in her third WNBA season and has already played in the postseason. Miles is a rookie and was experiencing playoff basketball for the first time.Miles did not hide her disappointment after the Lynx were eliminated. Speaking about her performance, she said:“Losing games is a part of it. Having games like I had is a part of it… Everyone wants to win all the time, but that’s not how it works… I have to remind myself that I’m a rookie, I’m not a 10-year vet. I have to remind myself I don’t know what I’m doing… Now, there’s no excuse… I’m ready to get it back.”The comments showed that Miles understands the gap between a strong regular season and the demands of the playoffs. articles.title: ‘That’s on Y’all’ — Deion Sanders Bluntly Reacts to Colorado’s Declining TV Ratings After Disappointing 2–2 Start
articles.summary: Deion Sanders can sell tickets, move television numbers, and turn a September press conference into a clip before lunch. None of that does much good when Col...
articles.body:
Deion Sanders can sell tickets, move television numbers, and turn a September press conference into a clip before lunch. None of that does much good when Colorado is sitting at 2-2.

So when Sanders was asked about the Buffaloes losing some of their television juice, Coach Prime made his priorities pretty clear. Nielsen can worry about Nielsen while he worries about getting Colorado back in the win column.

Deion Sanders Has Zero Interest in Winning the Ratings Battle

"Man, we ain't playing for no durn TV ratings. That's on y'all," Sanders said. "We don't care about no TV ratings."

The question did not come out of nowhere. Colorado became appointment television almost overnight when Sanders took over for the 2023 season, but the audience has cooled in the years since

ESPN games featuring Colorado averaged 6.1 million viewers in 2023, 3.4 million in 2024, and 2 million last season. That 67% slide already sparked plenty of discussion about whether the Prime Effect was starting to wear off before this season even began.

Sanders essentially answered that conversation with the scoreboard.

"TV ratings follow you when you win. They follow that," Sanders said.

He pointed to the crowd Colorado drew at Baylor and predicted another strong turnout when the Buffaloes return home this weekend. No. 12 Texas Tech visits Folsom Field for Homecoming on Saturday, giving Sanders a much bigger concern than who is holding the remote.

Sanders even turned the ratings discussion into a comedy bit.

PREDICT THE CFB SEASON: PFN's Free CFB Playoff Predictor

"Do they rate homes in the hood?" Sanders asked while wondering how Nielsen actually measures audiences. "I'm serious, straight up. Do they rate homes in the hood?"

Then he got back to the number he actually cares about.

"I'm not worried about no ratings, man. I'm worried about a durn record," Sanders said. "Like, I want to win. That's what I'm concerned with."

Colorado Needs Wins a Lot More Than It Needs Viewers

Colorado opened with wins over Georgia Tech and Weber State, then got blasted 41-7 by Northwestern before losing 23-13 at Baylor. The Buffaloes are now 0-1 in Big 12 play with an undefeated Texas Tech team coming to Boulder.

The underlying numbers are not helping Sanders sleep any easier. Colorado owns a 71.7 grade in PFN's CFB Offense Impact rankings, No. 89 nationally through four games.

The Buffaloes scored seven points against Northwestern and 13 against Baylor. They also have a quarterback decision hanging over the offense after Isaac Wilson replaced Julian Lewis during the Baylor loss.

Sanders is in his fourth season, making Colorado impossible to ignore. At 2-2, he would clearly trade a few million eyeballs for one more number in the win column.

articles.body:
Letters… we get letters… we get stacks and stacks of letters…

We can win with our freshman quarterback. We cannot win having punts blocked for an opposing team touchdown. Or running fale punts where only the punter knows its a fake. My question is, How can we stop doing stupid stuff?

PatrickSawyer: I … don't know. The "don't beat yourself then let Pavia Curtis go win it" game plan SHOULD still be in use. They seem to have lost their "do not commit dumb penalties" and "block everyone on special teams" situation sheets though. It is weird and confusing development.

Cole Sullivan : Look, these boys didn't come to Vandy to play school. Wait, some of them did? Oh, then why aren't they getting more un-stupider?…

Really, I don't know. Sometimes you're just gaffe-happy and I think that's just something we have to live with this year.

Andrew VU '04: Seeing as the only members of the team with fully developed frontal lobes are the coaches, they've got to be on top of ironing out our dumb-fuckery. Here's the thing, though. If all the "stupid stuff" was just rooking mistakes by a talented freshman QB, it would be much more forgivable than what it has been. To add to your list of special teams dumb-assery, I'm still not loving Beck's play-calling this year.

p.s. The phrase "stupid stuff" had this song playing in my head the entire time I was answering. Sure, the song is "morbid stuff," but other than the first syllable, it's the same, right?

I think it is generally assumed that losing Diego was the biggest loss in the off-season. What would you rank as the next biggest loss? Stowers, Tre Richardson, offensive line turnover (Henderson and Glass probably being the most important), or something else?

Tom Stephenson: It's probably the offensive line turnover, because this offensive line ain't it. Regardless of what you think about the skill players, this offense looks a lot different if Sedrick has room to run.

PatrickSawyer: Stowers or Richardson. Probably Richardson once Spence is back in full action. The lack of a real, defense-worrying deep threat is a problem. Curtis with his arm could take deep shots even with little time and let a speedster like that run under it. Stowers did drag a lot of attention, too.

Cole Sullivan : Stowers. He would open up a lot on plays he was never even going to be a threat in. There's a reason he is riding the IR in Philadelphia right now. He was fantastic at positioning himself around the ball and hauling things in when you were out of other options, which would be great for a quarterback whose finesse is still not quite finely tuned.

Andrew VU '04: Tre Richardson. Could you imagine what the cannon arm on The Courtesy Bear could do with a speed merchant like 3 son of Richard? Sure, you'd still need people to block for him, but we'd be seeing a hell of a lot fewer stacked boxes with the over-the-top thread of Thrice Dick's-child.

Other than Curtis, who is one player on the offense who needs to start becoming a difference maker for this team to have any chance at another win this year? Who needs to step up on defense to move the het-o-meter in a positive direction?

Tom Stephenson: I'm pretty much giving up on the offensive line, so I'm with Patrick and I'll say anybody in the WR room. In the modern game you just can't have an offense with one guy who can catch passes.

Defense? Yeah, I'm not sure what Outtara has been doing for a guy we were pretty excited about.

PatrickSawyer: Any WR or TE. Just need anyone except Sherrill to spread defenses out. I think spinning it as needing someone to step up to have any chance at another win is overly negative. Arkansas is still bad. State is literally just a QB. And I'm still not sold on Florida…or maybe Ole Miss used all their juice against Lane.

Defensively, maybe Outtara or Seabrooks. The edges have been decent enough. The interior rush has been lacking when not provided by LBs or Safeties. The real "fix" is more 2 or 3 guys to be just a tick better. Hight seems slightly off, and Ricardo Jones is clearly still settling in to the system.

Cole Sullivan : On offense, we really need Conner or Brown catching more balls if we are going to have a chance at scoring big if at all on some of these more fearsome SEC defenses. On defense, I think it's Ricardo Jones that I saw allow a few too many big plays in the Wolfpack Heart Attack game. He clutched up a little near the end, and he picked the ball 6 times last year, but so far this year he has not been able to put anything together. I don't even necessarily need him to be a difference maker, I just need him to make his tackles more consistently.

Andrew VU '04: On offense, Cheryl has been okay, but needed to level up to dominant for this offense to work. Other than that, pick an offensive lineman. On the other side, The Great Muppet Capers has stepped up time and time again. I'll agree with Patrick. The Outer Limits needs to eat more and clog up both arteries and running lanes.

It seems to me that the fake punt failure and the play calls getting to the huddle late are clearly coaching problems. The blocked punt and the failure to make a first down after first and five might also be coaching related. Do you think the coaching staff is capable of effectively addressing these issues and if they can adjust the offensive play calling to align with Curtis's skill set?

PatrickSawyer: I have no idea why plays are slow to come in. Curtis looks cool and calm doing almost everything. Let it rip.

The special teams disasters are just unfathomable.

Cole Sullivan : Yes, they are capable of it. Will they live up to their full potential? Change the logo.

Andrew VU '04: You certainly cannot have the "put them in position to punt" coaching philosophy and allow that to happen on two punt plays. Yeah… it hasn't looked great. I will say that part of the offensive coaching weirdness was the ridiculous QB competition farce from the spring until week 3 of the season. That Kill/Beck/Lea didn't plan the entire offense around our very own Nuke LaLoosh, or at least get him the football equivalent of Crash Davis… yeesh.

We've floated that Lea caught lightening in the bottle with Pavia, but what if it was Coaches Kill and Beck who did so with the offense? Between them (allegedly) pushing Blaze over Curtis and the playcalling in these first 4 games, were they Pavia merchants?

Tom Stephenson: I am not sure how after two games with a five-star quarterback starting for them you come to the conclusion that they were Pavia merchants. I mean, if they legitimately could only do what they did with Pavia and can't get that much out of a five-star NFL talent, yeah, fire them.

PatrickSawyer: A true freshman adjusting to the SEC (both starts were technically P4 opponents) after playing low level high school football. He's adjusting well, but it is a playbook that relies on the QB making 3 or 4 reads, whether those are in the option, RPO, or passing game, so it is a lor to digest and process. I think we are going to see the offense and Curtis continue to bloom together as the season progresses.

Cole Sullivan : I think Pavia was more important than the coaching staff that accompanied him (just like I think Brady was more important than Bellichick), but just like one of an exquisite wine and well-aged cheese tastes better than the other, the sensual delight of the two is maximized only once paired. Pavia and Beck and Kill all brought out the best in each other, truly greater than the sum of their parts. Maybe they can capture lightning in a bottle again (do you think they would reuse the same bottle, or try a new one? The former, you know it works. The latter, hey maybe the old one broke from all that lightning rattling around inside.) and if they can't, scraping a few wins together may be all we would get with anyone else in their positions anyways.

Andrew VU '04: What if it was all the "Party Rock" Juju from Pavia's brothers? I do think Pavia made their system hum, and further, defenses have adjusted to said system. Have you seen the Eagles' OC Sean Mannion repeatedly trying the "WR orbits around the QB while in motion and catches a screen pass" play to Makai Lemon this year? It's literally averaging negative yards… and they keep calling it! Feetball is a game of constant adjustments. Beck/Kill/Lea must counter. If you can't make a young Josh Allen fit into your offense, you change your offense to fit young Mr. Golden Arm.

Are we getting close to the "wait till basketball season" mindset?

Tom Stephenson: Well, at least we're not in the "wait 'till baseball season" mindset like we were for most of the Drew and Stackhouse eras…

…but also, yes, wake me up when we beat someone of note.

PatrickSawyer: Nah. I need more Curtis. Whatever the team and season may be, he is appointment viewing.

Cole Sullivan : Yes but not because we are suffering as much as usual but instead because our basketball teams are supposed to be just that good.

Andrew VU '04: No, and not just because we all have already seen a weird sunny outdoor game where we whupped up on the University of Virginny Wahoo-Cav-Happy Papis. I'm struggling to see more than 1-2 more wins this year, but I'm still looking forward to seeing how Curtis grows up against tough competition (you know, as long as Beck takes the training wheels off the offense). I've said it all year, but only because it's true. Expect growing pains with a side of Baby Josh Allen magic. If that's not exciting, then you got real complacent real quick after one 10 win season, i.e. Brigadoon #2.

That said, this year's Shooty Hoops team could be really special. Baseball's got some really interesting freshmen coming in, too. Lots to look forward to. Hail Pinman.

articles.title: Former K-State head coach Jerome Tang reaches settlement with university after firing
articles.summary: Former Kansas State head basketball coach Jerome Tang has reached a settlement with the university following his firing earlier this year.
articles.body:
MANHATTAN, Kan. — Former Kansas State head basketball coach Jerome Tang has reached a settlement with the university following his firing earlier this year .

According to reports, the school will pay Tang $12 million between now and the end of 2027. He was owed $18.7 million.

Tang was fired back in February after he called out his team, saying they didn't deserve to wear the K-State jersey, and removed the names from the backs of players' jerseys.

K-State Athletic Director said he was fired with cause and released the following statement:

This was a decision that was made in the best interest of our university and men's basketball program. Recent public comments and conduct, in addition to the program's overall direction, have not aligned with K-State's standards for supporting student-athletes and representing the university. We wish Coach Tang and his family all the best moving forward.

Tang's lawyer, Tom Mars, then sent a warning to Taylor and K-State School President Richard Linton after his firing.

"If K-State's President and AD really think the school was embarrassed by recent events, that's nothing compared to the embarrassment that both of them are about to experience," Mars said back in February.

Tang spent four seasons at K-State, going 71-57 and reaching the Elite Eight in his first season with the program, and winning over the fanbase with his energetic personality. He then signed a seven-year contract extension in 2023.

K-State failed to reach the tournament over the next three seasons, as the relationship between Tang and the school soured.

Tang is now an associate head coach for the second time at Baylor University.

articles.title: Pro wrestling returns to Springfield’s Shrine Mosque, a haven for wrestling history
articles.summary: Mid-States Wrestling is scheduled to bring its Wrestling at the Shrine event to the historic Springfield Shrine Mosque on Saturday, Oct. 3.
articles.body:
SPRINGFIELD, Mo. — The chairs will be set up. The ring will go in the middle of the floor. And on Saturday night, professional wrestling will return to one of Springfield's most historic wrestling venues.

Mid-States Wrestling is bringing its "Wrestling at the Shrine" event back to the Shrine Mosque, a building that has played host to generations of wrestling fans and some of the sport's biggest stars. Keep reading for a wrestling history lesson, and watch the video at the top of this page to see an interview and vintage archived footage.

For Space Cowboy Jason Jones, the return is about more than putting on another wrestling show. It's personal.

Jones has been wrestling for 30 years and promotes Mid-States Wrestling, which puts on shows throughout Missouri, Arkansas and the Mid-South.

His connection to the Shrine Mosque goes back to his childhood.

"My relationship with my father going here and then to be able to come here and actually promote an event with Mid-State Wrestling, it's full circle," Jones said. "And we want to create those memories that I got to create with my father."

Jones remembers coming to the Shrine as a 6- or 7-year-old and watching some of professional wrestling's biggest names.

Ric Flair. The Road Warriors. Dusty Rhodes.

At the time, the Shrine was part of the circuit for the National Wrestling Alliance, before later becoming a stop for World Championship Wrestling and eventually WWE.

"We saw Flair, we saw Steamboat, we saw Steve Austin back, you know, in the day, and Sting," Jones said. "Sting was such a big name here, the Junkyard Dog and all those greats that came through here. All the way up to WWE."

For younger wrestlers like Colton Theron Vaught, known as "Must CTV," the Shrine's history is part of what makes stepping into the ring there so meaningful.

Vaught is an MMA fighter and professional wrestler who recently returned from a WWE tryout during SummerSlam weekend in Minneapolis in August.

He said the experience put him around some of the most recognizable names in the business, including Shawn Michaels, William Regal and X-Pac.

"They were helping give me all this information," Vaught said. "I learned so much that it was absolutely incredible. And so I'm happy to implement everything that I've learned there and take it here to the Shrine."

But Vaught already had a personal connection to the building long before he ever had the chance to wrestle inside it.

One of his strongest Shrine memories involves WWE Hall of Famer Eddie Guerrero.

Guerrero had defeated Brock Lesnar to win a championship, and one of his first appearances afterward was at the Shrine Mosque. Vaught wanted to be there, but couldn't make the trip.

"It's almost like I'm fulfilling that to now be able to wrestle here and get to see what I didn't get to see Eddie do many years back here," Vaught said.

The building also has a direct connection to Vaught's own wrestling lineage.

His trainer was WWE Hall of Famer Harley Race, an eight-time NWA World Champion. Race also wrestled in the Shrine Mosque during the building's heyday.

"One of the title changes happened right here, man," Vaught said. "So it's an incredible venue."

Race also defended the title at the Shrine Mosque, with a defense over David Von Erich in May of 1980.

For longtime Springfield wrestling fans, the memories go even deeper.

"When you talk to people of a certain age, they all have those memories of turning on, watching the television show that was filmed here Wednesday nights," Jones said.

Names like Danny Hodge, Skandor Akbar, Bulldog Bob Brown and Harley Race still come up. Cowboy Bill Watts and other wrestling legends also made their mark at the Shrine.

WWE Hall of Famer Cowboy Bob Orton will be in attendance Saturday, along with WWE Hall of Famer The Godfather, who also wrestled as Papa Shango in WWE.

Now, a new generation of wrestlers is hoping to add its own memories to the building's history.

For Jones, bringing Mid-States Wrestling back to the Shrine is ultimately about reconnecting Springfield with a piece of its past.

"We're bringing back wrestling, the historic Shrine," Jones said.

And for the wrestlers who will enter the ring Saturday, the goal is to make sure the next generation has stories of its own to tell.

"We're so excited and honored to be here more than anything," Jones said.

Mid-State Wrestling's "Wrestling at the Shrine" is scheduled for Saturday, Oct. 3. Doors open at 5:30 p.m., with the event beginning at 7 p.m.

Tickets for the event are available here.

articles.body:
A new concern emerges for the Chicago Bears heading into their Week 4 battle against the New York Jets on Sunday at Soldier Field.

Chicago released its latest injury report Thursday, and quarterback Caleb Williams is still unable to practice.

That's not entirely surprising, as he continues to deal with a hamstring injury that forced him to miss Week 3's game against the Philadelphia Eagles, but the sudden appearance of running back D'Andre Swift on the injury report due to a knee issue may sound alarming.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Swift has been instrumental to the early-season success of the Bears. He had an outstanding season debut in Chicago's 59-37 Week 1 shootout win over the Carolina Panthers, rushing for 124 yards and three touchdowns.

The former Georgia Bulldogs star tailback was much quieter in Week 2's 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings at home, with 45 receiving yards and zero touchdowns on 16 carries, before recording 84 rushing yards with no scores on 20 carries in Chicago's 27-7 victory over the Eagles at home.

The Bears still have one more day of practice left before taking on New York. Friday's practice session can be very telling of what Swift's status will be for Sunday's game.

An absence by Swift in Week 4 could mean a whole lot more work for Kyle Monangai.

Swift leads the Bears this season with 253 rushing yards to go with three touchdowns on 54 carries, while Monangai is right behind him with 178 rushing yards and a touchdown on 30 rushing attempts.

As a team, Chicago is leading the league entering Week 4 with an average of 184.3 rushing yards per game.

The Eagles ' offense got a major offseason re-design. Through three games, there's still clear issues to be worked out, including health concerns.

With running back Saquon Barkley yet to score a touchdown this season, and tight end Dallas Goedert sidelined with a knee injury, it appears the Eagles' depth will be tested even more in Week 4 with news on lead wide receiver DeVonta Smith on Thursday.

With Smith looking unlikely to play in Week 4, the Eagles will be turning to some more unproven depth options at wide receiver, with former Packer Dontayvion Wicks leading the way.

Wicks has established himself as the No. 2 to Smith early in the season, impressing with his separation and catching nine passes for 179 yards and a touchdown. He's likely first in line to see an uptick in targets against the Rams without Smith.

It could also be a good opportunity, however, for first-round pick Makai Lemon to have a breakout game. articles.body:
Welcome back to another edition of NHL Rumours from the crew at Last Word on Hockey. The puck has been dropped, and the 2026-27 regular season is now underway. However, that doesn't mean that the rumours will stop. If anything, they will continue to heat up as teams get a look at their rosters and figure out where they stand against the opposition and where improvements can be made. One of those teams is the Edmonton Oilers. In this edition of NHL Rumours, we focus on the team's interest in current Montreal Canadiens forward Kirby Dach .

All NHL rumours come from their original source and are subject to change.

NHL Rumours: Oilers Showing Interest in Canadiens Forward as the Season Opens

Rumour: According to Frank Seravalli, the Oilers have a serious interest in Canadiens forward Kirby Dach.

Analysis: As Seravalli explains it, the Oilers' interest in Dach borders on drooling. They have a desperate need for a right-shot centreman, and Dach certainly provides that. Currently, the only right-shot centreman on the Oilers roster is rookie Owen Michaels , who just competed in his first NHL game on Tuesday night. Adding Dach would give them a much more proven option and someone who could certainly benefit from a change of scenery.

Dach has found himself falling out of favour in Montreal. When the Canadiens acquired him, the thought was that he would be the perfect number two centre behind Nick Suzuki . However, due to multiple injuries and inconsistent play, Dach has been passed on the depth chart by Alex Newhook , who is currently operating as the 2C. With Phillip Danault and Jake Evans occupying the centre ice position on the other two lines, Dach is now slotting in on the right side next to Danault. While this isn't a major issue, as it shows Dach's versatility and how much depth the Canadiens have to be able to deploy their lineup this way, it begs the question of where the Canadiens see Dach in their lineup moving forward. Hence the interest from the Oilers.

There could be a potential homecoming for Dach if he is dealt to the Oilers. Dach is originally from Fort Saskatchewan, which is about 30 minutes outside of Edmonton. Going home to play for what is essentially your hometown team would certainly be something of interest for the 25-year-old centreman. Not to mention, his younger brother Colton is already on the roster. The chance to go home and play with his brother is certainly something that would be a dream come true for Dach.

The Canadiens are going to be faced with a big decision regarding Dach. They signed him to a one-year contract this offseason. At season's end, he will be an unrestricted free agent. Depending on how the season goes for Dach, he could earn himself another deal, but is that something he is going to want? Potentially, especially after the run the Canadiens went on last year. However, if there's an opportunity to go home for more money and play next to his brother, he might just be enticed to leave, and the Canadiens would lose him for nothing. Will the Canadiens use him as their own rental player as they try to make another run at Lord Stanley's Cup this season, or would they be better off trading him before the deadline, getting something in return for the big, versatile forward? This is a storyline to certainly follow as the season goes on.

articles.title: Patriots rooting guide for NFL Week 4
articles.summary: Rooting information, kickoff times, TV schedule and more for NFL Week 4.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots will attempt to get back to .500 on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET against the Buffalo Bills, trying to improve to 2-2 on the year. While our focus is on this specific game, it is only one of 16 on the menu in Week 4 of the 2026 NFL regular season.

Here is who to root for in the other 15 not featuring the Patriots.

Pittsburgh Steelers (2-1) at Cleveland Browns (2-1): Go Steelers! The Patriots have already beaten the Steelers, which means they hold the head-to-head tiebreaker and a Pittsburgh win would boost their strength of schedule and victory tiebreakers. | Prime Video

Indianapolis Colts (1-2) at Washington Commanders (1-2): Go Commanders! The classic case of picking the NFC team over the AFC team with no other direct ties to the Patriots. | NFL Network

Tennessee Titans (0-3) at Baltimore Ravens (2-1): Go Titans! For the sake of the Patriots' standing in the AFC playoff race, we will obviously go with the worse-ranked team here. | CBS

New York Jets (1-2) at Chicago Bears (2-1): Go Bears! With Patriots' highest fifth-round pick going to Philadelphia anyway as part of the A.J. Brown trade, there are no implications should Chicago win. But even if that were not the case, we would still go NFC team over AFC team here. | FOX

Jacksonville Jaguars (2-1) at Cincinnati Bengals (2-1): Go Bengals! Somebody has to win, so it might just be the team that does not have the head-to-head advantage over the Patriots. New England needs to win more games than Jacksonville to finish ahead in the playoff standings. | CBS

Dallas Cowboys (1-2) at Houston Texans (0-3): Go Cowboys! A Cowboys win would kill two birds with one stone for the Patriots: it will keep an AFC rival down and possibly end up improving the position of the sixth-round draft pick acquired in the Marte Mapu trade. | FOX

Arizona Cardinals (1-2) at New York Giants (2-1): Go good game! Two NFC teams clashing with no impact on the Patriots. | CBS

Los Angeles Rams (1-2) at Philadelphia Eagles (2-1): Go good game! Same as above. | FOX

Green Bay Packers (1-2) at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-3): Go Packers! Three words: strength of schedule. | FOX

Miami Dolphins (0-3) at Minnesota Vikings (3-0): Go Vikings! Strength of schedule does not matter in this game given that the Patriots play both of those teams this year. What does matter is the Dolphins dropping to 0-4 against an NFC team. | FOX

Kansas City Chiefs (3-0) at Las Vegas Raiders (3-0): Go Raiders! Both teams are unbeaten and on New England's schedule, with Kansas City looking like the safer bet to be a serious playoff contender in the AFC this year. In that case, a loss by them would be the preferred outcome. | CBS

Los Angeles Chargers (0-3) at Seattle Seahawks (2-1): Go Seahawks! With both teams on the Patriots' schedule this year, we will pick the NFC team over the AFC team. Yes, it might end up hurting New England's strength of victory, but even with the Chargers at 0-3 the season is still too young to write them off just yet. | CBS

Denver Broncos (2-1) at San Francisco 49ers (3-0): Go Niners! NFC team over AFC team, even if it ends up hurting New England's strength of schedule. | CBS

Detroit Lions (2-1) at Carolina Panthers (1-2): Go good game! Two NFC teams with no direct ties to the Patriots going at each other. Just sit back, relax, and enjoy. | NBC

Atlanta Falcons (1-2) at New Orleans Saints (1-2): Go Falcons! The Patriots own the Saints' sixth-round pick next year from the Ja'Lynn Polk trade, so every New Orleans loss helps boost that pick's value. | ESPN

articles.title: Klopp gets off the mark as Germany beat Serbia
articles.summary: Jurgen Klopp finally secured his first victory as Germany manager as his side beat Serbia 2-0 in Munich, easing some pressure after a difficult start to his...
articles.body:
Jurgen Klopp finally secured his first victory as Germany manager as his side beat Serbia 2-0 in Munich, easing some pressure after a difficult start to his reign.

Klopp made wholesale changes following defeat by Greece, but Germany quickly established control. Serge Gnabry and Nick Woltemade both threatened before Tom Bischof opened the scoring shortly before half-time.

Florian Wirtz was central to the breakthrough, weaving through the Serbian defence before seeing his effort rebound off the post. Bischof reacted quickest to smash the loose ball into the roof of the net for his first international goal.

Germany continued to dominate after the restart, although their finishing remained inconsistent. Woltemade somehow missed from close range, while Derry Scherhant also went close on his debut.

The hosts eventually found a second in the 60th minute. Maximilian Mittelstadt picked out Wirtz, who turned brilliantly inside the area before firing into the bottom corner.

Serbia offered little in response as Germany comfortably controlled the closing stages, leaving Klopp with his first win after three matches in charge.

articles.summary: Troy Parrott scored twice, but the Republic of Ireland surrendered a two-goal lead as Austria fought back to earn a 2-2 draw in Dublin.Ireland made the perfe...
articles.body:
Troy Parrott scored twice, but the Republic of Ireland surrendered a two-goal lead as Austria fought back to earn a 2-2 draw in Dublin.

Ireland made the perfect start when Parrott produced an excellent individual run, beating two defenders before calmly finishing past Florian Wiegele .

The game was twice briefly stopped in the first half after protests. Tennis balls carrying Palestinian flags and messages calling for the game to be stopped were thrown onto the pitch, while a protester later entered the field before being removed by security.

Ireland doubled their advantage before half-time when Ryan Manning was fouled inside the area. Parrott stepped up and confidently converted the resulting penalty.

Austria responded strongly after the break, with substitute Alexander Prass reducing the deficit after Liam Kitching gave the ball away.

The visitors completed their comeback five minutes later. Michael Gregoritsch curled a free-kick beyond Caoimhin Kelleher to level the scores.

Ireland struggled to regain control in the closing stages, but held on for a point. Austria remain top of Group B3, while Ireland sit third and are unbeaten in nine matches at the Aviva Stadium.

articles.title: Jordan Smith makes walk-off albatross to tie for Bank of Utah Championship lead
articles.summary: A final-hole 2 lifted Jordan Smith into a five-way tie for the lead at Black Desert Resort in Ivins, Utah.
articles.body:
It was a tale of two golfers late in the day Thursday at the Bank of Utah Championship .

Birdies and eagles were flying all over the Tom Weiskopf-designed Black Desert Resort in Ivins, Utah. But the shot of the day came courtesy of Jordan Smith.

After back-to-back birdies on Nos. 7 and 8 (he started at the 10th) Smith was 238 yards out after a 350-yard drive. From there, his second shot just cleared a greenside bunker and then rolled up to the cup, gently clinking the flagstick before dropping down for a 2 on the par 5. Yes, it was a rare albatross, made even moreso as it came on the final hole of his round.

The PGA Tour reports that it's the fifth albatross of the season and first since Davis Thompson had one in the third round of the Wyndham Championship.

Smith then played spectator as Brendon Todd and Mackenzie Hughes finished their rounds.

That capped off an 8-under 63 for Smith, and vaulted him into a five-way tie for the lead. He is 69th in the FedEx Cup Fall standings and is among those fighting to climb inside the top 60 for 2027. He's well on his way to do just that.

2026 Bank of Utah Championship scores, live updates for Thursday's Round 1

Then we have Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen. He opened double bogey-par-double bogey and was going the wrong way on the leaderboard. He started on the back nine and was just 3 over at the turn but he then doubled the second. A pair of pars came before disaster struck: a quintuple 9 on the par-4 fifth hole.

It was shortly after that that Neergaard-Petersen became the second withdrawal of the day, with his WD coming due to illness.

That leaves the field with 119 golfers for the rest of Thursday and Friday.
